detail.longDescription: I have an Azure DevOps pipeline that needs to check whether a self-hosted agent with specific capabilities is online before queuing a deployment: steps: - task: PowerShell@2 displayName: 'List visible agent pools' inputs: targetType: inline errorActionPreference: stop script: | $collectionUri = "$(System.CollectionUri)" $headers = @{ Authorization = "Bearer $env:SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN" } $who = Invoke-RestMethod ` -Uri "${collectionUri}_apis/connectiondata?api-version=7.1-preview" ` -Headers $headers $allPools = Invoke-RestMethod ` -Uri "${collectionUri}_apis/distributedtask/pools?api-version=7.1" ` -Headers $headers Write-Host "Pools visible to this identity (count: $($allPools.count)):" $allPools.value | ForEach-Object { Write-Host " id=$($_.id) name='$($_.name)'" } $pool = Invoke-RestMethod ` -Uri "${collectionUri}_apis/distributedtask/pools?poolName=$env:TARGET_POOL&api-version=7.1" ` -Headers $headers Write-Host "Filtered lookup response: $($pool | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5 -Compress)" env: SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN: $(System.AccessToken) TARGET_POOL: '<pool>' Pools visible to this identity (count: 0): Filtered lookup response: {"count":0,"value":[]} Problem is the output above. I tried adding Project Collection Build Service Accounts as an administrator in the project Agent Pool -> <pool> -> Security Settings but that didn't fix it. What do I need to do in order to let the pipeline's request see the pools? Or more specific, this pool I am trying to target that has multiple agents. The rest of the pipeline is able to use this pool.
